Not for redistribution without written consent of Morgan Stanley Morgan Stanley RESEARCH November 5, 2025 01:28 AM GMT Alphabet Inc. | North America Why Google Cloud Could Grow 50%+ in '26 New/updated Google Cloud Backlog model outlines path to 50%+ Google Cloud revenue growth in '26, which would be mid single digit+ % upside to us and 15%+ upside to Street. We view Google Cloud growth as continued driver of GOOGL multiple expansion and AI-driven outperformance. Remain OW, $330 PT. We Introduce a New Cloud Backlog Model...We introduce a new/updated Cloud backlog model breaking down Google Cloud's growth across backlog and non-backlog workloads (on demand). GOOGL disclosed that ~55% of its $158bn backlog in 3Q25 is expected to be recognized as revenue in the next 2 years. We also incorporated the history of this quarterly forward 2 year recognition within our model. This implies that the backlog has driven a relatively consistent ~45-50% of Google Cloud revenue (with the remainder driven by on demand workloads). This also means that GOOGL's on demand business grew 29%/37% y/y in '23/'24 and has grown ~25% YTD in '25 ...Highlighting The Potential for Google Cloud to Grow Revenue 50%+ in 2026: With these inputs, in Exhibit 1 , we sensitize backlog Y/Y dollar growth and on demand Y/Y percentage revenue growth to show the potential for substantial upside to our base case ~44% Y/Y '26 Google Cloud growth. As shown, the extent to which GOOGL can add ~$50bn+ in net backlog in '26 (a notable step down from the chunky surging ~$106bn we expect them to add in '25) and the on demand business can grow ~15%+ would translate into 50%+ growth for Google Cloud. Even the on demand business continuing to grow at 25% Y/Y growth and a $20bn step-up in backlog can translate into 50%+ growth. This would represent mid single digit+ % upside to our current base case estimate and ~15%+ upside to current Street consensus. Please let us know if you would like our Google Cloud backlog model. Source: Company data, Morgan Stanley Research Where Could We Be Wrong to the Upside? Greater Than Expected Dollar Backlog Growth: Our base case assumes a conservative $20bn net added to GOOGL Cloud backlog in '26 (a steep deceleration from the $106bn that we estimate could be added in '25). The extent to which the pace of backlog deals signed grows more than we expect could be a significant driver of upside to our numbers, as we estimate every additional $20bn added to '26 net backlog growth could drive an additional ~340bps upside to '26 Google Cloud revenue growth. • Faster than Expected Growth in On Demand Business: Given the recent large-scale cloud deals signed, we assume GOOGL Cloud sees a significant mix shift toward backlog-driven revenue (with our base case implying backlog constitutes ~60% of '26 Google Cloud revenue where historically backlog has made up around ~45-50%). However, the extent to which we overestimate this mix shift progression could actually lead to further upside to our Google Cloud revenue. We estimate every additional 1000bps of growth in non-backlog revenue in '26 could add ~500bps to '26 Google Cloud revenue growth. Where Could We Be Wrong to the Downside? Anthropic Already in Backlog as of 3Q?: Our base case assumes GOOGL's gross backlog grows by ~$50bn in 4Q25 to account for the recent Anthropic deal. If that number proves to be too high for any reason (Anthropic already reflected in the 3Q:25 backlog, or the size of the Anthropic deal is smaller than expected, or a slower than anticipated pipeline of deals to come), it could lead to slower Google Cloud growth ahead (all else equal). • Timing Dynamics Could Reduce Predictability: We assume that the forward backlog waterfalls into GOOGL revenue on a largely consistent basis over the 2 year time horizon (assuming ~50-55% of backlog is recognized over the

BASE CASE
Faster innovation and Search/GCP acceleration lead to multiple expansion and higher earnings power. Search revenue accelerates as AI-driven innovation delivers meaningful upside to engagement. New AI offerings prove incremental to the top and bottom line and don't cannibalize core Search. YouTube and Cloud become even bigger contributors to top-line growth, and operate at a higher margin than in our base case.
$330.00 BEAR CASE

Assumes pragmatic search revenue growth in '26, continued incremental platform monetization and Google Cloud acceleration in '26. As GOOGL continues platform-level innovation on Search and other categories, we assume pragmatic revenue/EBITDA growth. GOOGL introduces new AI offerings which increase con dence in the durability of long term growth and calm fears around competition. Google Cloud accelerates fidriven by new partnerships and growing backlog.
$200.00

New AI products create greater than expected margin pressure due to lower monetization rates and increased compute intensity.
